quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. How can you prevent hydroplaning in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep your speed the same.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In rain, slow down to reduce hydroplaning risk. Driving too fast can make your tires ride on water and lose contact with the road. This makes your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate. Once the gate is up, only cross the tracks if you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: When must vehicles have liability insurance?

options.text: Only on interstates.
Only when driven by a minor.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: State law requires all motor vehicles to have liability insurance at all times. This protects people in case of an accident.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually what color and must always be obeyed?

options.text: White
Blue
Green

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are white with black markings. Drivers must obey them.

questions.question: A steady yellow light warns that red is coming. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Keep moving and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep moving and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, clear it as fast as you safely can.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop completely.
Drive at your normal speed.
Slow down and be careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. Stay alert as you approach.

questions.question: When should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your car.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your car.
questions.explanation: In rain, snow, or fog, it is hard for other drivers to see your vehicle. Headlights make your car easier to see. If you need windshield wipers, you must use your headlights too.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Neither lane can pass.
Both lanes can pass.
Only the right lane can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate traffic going in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: How should you yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to emergency vehicles by driving to the right edge and stopping. Avoid stopping in an intersection. You can move again after it passes.

questions.question: Your reaction time becomes slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your vision and alertness. As you drink more, your judgment and driving skills get worse. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and other vehicles.

questions.question: What does a green traffic signal tell drivers to do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Go straight, turn left, or turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight, turn left, or turn right.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go straight or turn where allowed. When turning, you must first yield to pedestrians or vehicles lawfully in the intersection.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you cannot see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, do not return to your lane until you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle on the road?

options.text: Keep the posted speed to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Shift to neutral as you drive through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery surfaces like puddles to prevent skidding. A dry, solid road is the safest place to drive.

questions.question: If your car's rear end skids to the left, which way should you steer?

options.text: To the right.
To the left.
Tap the brakes lightly and shift to neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the left.
questions.explanation: In a skid, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This brings the front in line with the rear and straightens the vehicle.

questions.question: How can you help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning can cause you to skid.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus is picking up or dropping off children?

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are going.
Stop if you are going the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are going.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off passengers, you must come to a complete stop before reaching the bus, regardless of which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up so you can turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. You cannot turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill with or without a curb, or uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge so your car rolls away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill with a curb, turn toward the center so your car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is beginning.

questions.question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, what should drivers do?

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk or sidewalk area when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and other traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended and red lights flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on its left.
Continue driving when you think most children are done exiting the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: Come to a complete stop when you see a school bus stopped with its stop signal arm extended and red lights flashing. Stay stopped until the stop signal is retracted and the red lights turn off.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.
Not permitted from either direction.
Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, passing is allowed from the side with the broken line. Passing is not allowed from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Yield the right-of-way.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets and roads where you cannot enter. You may see it if you try to enter an expressway ramp in the wrong direction.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in the fog.
Staring at the road ahead of your vehicle.
Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware of hazards. Staring only at the road ahead is dangerous. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beam headlights.

questions.question: What is the law about posters and signs on car windows?

options.text: They are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.
They are prohibited by state law if they obstruct a driver's view of the road.
They are allowed only if they do not contain offensive language.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are prohibited by state law if they obstruct a driver's view of the road.
questions.explanation: State law prohibits window obstructions. No sign, poster, or material can be placed on any vehicle window if it blocks a driver's clear view of the road.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Try to fight it.
Take a break.
Take some caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, go to the first available rest stop or service area to take a break, nap, stretch, or change drivers. Caffeine pills are not a replacement for rest and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
Your front wheels should be parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and leave your vehicle in park when parked on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels so the vehicle rolls away from traffic if the brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn wheels toward it when facing downhill or gently touching it when facing uphill.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Upcoming sharp left and right turns.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of an upcoming winding road. Adjust your speed as needed.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, park with all four wheels off the main part of the road when possible.

questions.question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:

options.text: No different than normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Keep an increased following distance when driving on slippery roads.

questions.question: When may you pass a vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross to change lanes. A dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the lane with the broken line, not from the solid line. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see clearly, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor due to darkness or bad weather, increase your following distance. This gives you more time to react to hazards you may not see ahead.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: To speed up slightly.
That it is not safe to pass.
To maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot legally pass in that area. You are likely in a place with limited visibility where passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: If vehicles constantly pass you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the lane on your right.
Move to the lane on your left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the lane on your right.
questions.explanation: On a road with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes except when passing or turning left. On an interstate highway, use the right lane if you are driving slower than the traffic around you.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn and maintain your speed.
Speed up to clear the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: When involved in a collision, what should you do with injured people?

options.text: Avoid moving them unless absolutely necessary.
Move them to their desired location.
Tell them they are fine without immediate medical attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid moving them unless absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people. Only move them if they are in danger from fire or other hazards. Keep them sitting or lying down until medical help arrives.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches you?

options.text: Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
Continue driving, but try to stay out of its way.
See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle displays flashing red or blue lights and is using its siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop completely. Do not try to drive faster than the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: You are in the left lane of a two-lane road with many vehicles passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane so you don't block traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move into the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than nearby traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: When you are behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Allow a larger following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a larger following distance.
questions.explanation: Keep at least three to four seconds of following distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly, and following too closely endangers both riders. If a motorcycle falls, you need extra space to avoid the rider. Falls are most likely on wet or icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.
